A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 43-page study, including Appendices A–F. Pagewise text and rendering comparisons establish that the paper content is identical; only the first-page arXiv version/date stamp and its link differ.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments on five LLaMA models, token-level analyses, and parameter-restoration results, including supplementary experiments in Appendices C and E.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original experimental results in the main text and Appendices C and E.

M1.justification: Mastery-based data categorization, top-10-logit normalization, and restoration of parameters ranked by relative change are identical in both versions.

E1.justification: Both use ENTITYQUESTIONS with the same 10 in-domain and 14 out-of-domain topics, plus XSum summarization and GSM8K mathematics evaluations in Table 5.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators are unchanged. Appendix C.3 and Table 7 retain LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct, SFT (Mixed), SFT (Divided), and LoRA alongside parameter restoration.

E3.justification: The model configurations, data sizes, splits, metrics, and testing procedures match. Section 3.3 retains batch size 8, one epoch, AdamW, and learning rate 1e-5.

E4.justification: Both retain the same data-scale and mastery analyses, restoration sweeps, training-set analysis in Appendix C.2, and layer/module analyses in Appendix E.

E5.justification: Repeated-run statements and mean/variance reporting in Sections 3.3–3.4 are identical. No uncertainty reporting or statistical procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: All reported values, trends, and rankings match across the main text and appendices. For example, Table 7 reports parameter-restoration accuracies of 62.21 in-domain and 57.10 out-of-domain in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of mastery groups, mastery probability, KL divergence, and relative parameter change are identical, including Appendices B.2 and F.1.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about data scale and mastery, unnecessary SFT updates, and the benefits of parameter restoration.

C2.justification: Explanations of knowledge shifts, forgetting, and layer-specific redundancy are unchanged. Both retain the same limitations concerning model-family coverage and the absence of a new efficient fine-tuning strategy.

D1.justification: Training and decoding details, the SFT prompt, restoration calculations, synonym mappings, and all topic templates remain identical in Section 3.3 and Appendices A, B, and F.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations, and references are identical. Neither the cited works nor the paper's positioning relative to prior research changes.

P1.justification: Only the marginal arXiv stamp changes from v1, dated 20 Sep 2025, to v2, dated 10 Feb 2026. Body wording, headings, and document structure are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–6, Tables 1–36, captions, and page layouts are unchanged. Rendering differences are confined to the version/date characters in the first-page margin.

improvement.justification: The main text and complete appendices preserve identical methods, evidence, claims, explanations, and technical details. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp and its link does not meaningfully improve or weaken the paper.
